newsitem.title: USA: Democrat takes lead in Colorado Senate race.
newsitem.headline: Democrat takes lead in Colorado Senate race.

text.p: The Democratic candidate for an open Senate seat in Colorado has pushed into the lead ahead of his Republican rival, but statistically the race is still too close to call, according to a poll published Wednesday.
In a poll of 500 registered voters who say they are likely to vote, Democrat Tom Strickland was leading Republican Wayne Allard by 51 percent to 45 percent.
The Bullet Poll was taken Sunday and Monday for KUSA-TV and published in The Denver Post. It has a margin of error of 4.5 percent.

The poll marks the first time in the survey since Sept. 30 that Strickland, a millionaire attorney, has moved ahead of Allard, who now represents Colorado's fourth congressional district in the U.S. House.
The hotly contested race is for the Senate seat being vacated by Republican Hank Brown.
